measurements.evidence: One of our newest residences, StuVi-2 accommodates 960 residents in two, unique high-rises. The 26-story north tower hosts juniors and seniors in an apartment-style setting, and the 19-story south tower houses sophomores, juniors, and seniors in a suite-style setting.

Tower A is the first phase of a $550 million overhaul of Warren Towers, BU’s largest residence hall and the second-largest nonmilitary dorm in the country. The complex, which houses 1,800 students per year, comprises three 18-story towers and opened in the mid-1960s. Klinger describes Warren as “an extraordinary asset” for the University, given its central location and the fact that so many undergraduates pass through its doors every year.

Built in 1963 and 1964 and last renovated from 2010 to 2012, the three 13-story residential towers, named for Boston University’s founders, Isaac Rich, Jacob Sleeper, and Lee Claflin, today are home to approximately 1,800 students.

Tucked just a block away from the bustle of Comm Ave, The Towers , the dorm-style residence hall at 140 Bay State Road, is conveniently located next to the Questrom School of Business and the Metcalf Center for Science & Engineering. Built in 1957, the building comprises two nine-story towers—East and West—connected by a common area. Home to 521 students, the dorm features double rooms on single-gender floors, as well as specialty floors for students enrolled in Questrom, the College of Engineering, and the College of Health & Rehabilitation Sciences: Sargent College.

Myles Standish Hall and Annex Renovation, 610-632 Beacon Street Myles Standish Hall was originally constructed in 1927 as a suite -style hotel and has been used by BU for undergraduate housing since 1949. Together with the Myles Standish Annex, which was acquired in 1980, the complex provided 760 student bed spaces. The renovation of the Myles Standish Hall and Annex maintained the historic structure while adapting the building to meet contemporary housing needs and accessibility. The renovation maximized bed count and private bedrooms, as well as implementing modern amenities, to provide space for 730 students
